image_description: A side-front view of a vintage-style minibus parked on a paved street. The vehicle has a two-tone color scheme (beige/cream lower, white upper) with red and black graphics. It features a boxy shape, large windshield, side windows, and visible wheels. There is text on the front destination board and side panels. A tripod stand is visible in the foreground left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits a distinct boxy silhouette typical of minibuses. Its proportions relative to the background buildings and wheel size confirm it is shorter than a full-size city bus but retains significant height.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, split-pane windshield is clearly visible at the front. A continuous row of rectangular side windows runs along the passenger compartment, consistent with minibus design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has substantial height. While the specific mechanism of the door is hard to discern due to image quality, the panel lines near the front wheel arch suggest a forward-mounted entrance door, which is standard for this class.

While the location of the door is inferable, the specific mechanical type (sliding vs. folding) cannot be definitively verified from this static, low-resolution angle as the door is closed and details are blurred.
There is a distinct hood/bonnet section ahead of the windshield and driver's cabin, indicating a front-engine layout typical of van-derived minibuses.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is completely occluded by the viewing angle; only the side and front are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus features a clear two-tone livery (cream/beige and white) with red graphical stripes and text, fitting the description of company/route markings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wheels are proportional to a light commercial vehicle/minibus. They appear to have standard dark steel rims, consistent with the vehicle class.
Based on the number of side windows (approx. 3-4 visible on this side) and overall length, the capacity aligns with the 4-10 passenger range typical for minibuses.

artifact_observations.location: Front destination header and side panel text
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the destination blind above the windshield and the red lettering on the side panel is illegible and structurally nonsensical. Characters appear melted or fused together, lacking the sharp edges of real printed signage.

Reflections in the side windows are inconsistent with the environment. Some window panes appear opaque or smeared rather than transparent, and the B-pillars between windows show slight warping and uneven thickness.

The front bumper area lacks clear definition. The headlight on the right side blends into the bodywork without a clear bezel or housing edge, suggesting a minor fusion artifact common in AI generations of complex mechanical parts.

The tripod stand in the bottom left has legs that seem to merge slightly with the pavement texture, and the perspective lines of the road markings are slightly inconsistent with the vehicle's orientation.

Structural integrity of front bumper and headlight housings

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text artifacts. In AI-generated images, text is often a primary failure mode. If the fine_grained_classifier confirms 'minibus' but the text auditor finds complete gibberish, the alignment score should remain high (as the object is correct) but the artifact score must reflect the visual noise. Also, verify if the 'melting' of the headlight into the bumper is a severe structural defect or just a low-resolution blur.
